subject.title: Feature: post-process NO_REPLY to suppress partial leaks

question: Should mixed-content output that ends with `NO_REPLY` be treated as whole-payload silence, or should OpenClaw keep preserving substantive-looking text except for narrower reasoning/silent-intent cases?
rationale: Current source and tests intentionally preserve ordinary substantive text before a trailing sentinel, while the issue describes a security-sensitive leak class; automation should not choose the privacy-versus-message-delivery boundary without maintainer intent.

options.title: Adopt a narrow shared classifier
options.body: Suppress reasoning, silent-intent, and internal-summary payloads consistently while preserving ordinary substantive replies that only mention or accidentally end with `NO_REPLY`.

options.title: Suppress any trailing sentinel
options.body: Treat any trailing or own-line `NO_REPLY` as whole-payload silence, accepting possible loss of legitimate replies that current tests preserve.

options.title: Keep current semantics
options.body: Leave generic mixed-content behavior unchanged and limit cleanup to already-fixed narrower token-only and reasoning-prefixed leaks.

recommendation.title: Adopt a narrow shared classifier
recommendation.body: Suppress reasoning, silent-intent, and internal-summary payloads consistently while preserving ordinary substantive replies that only mention or accidentally end with `NO_REPLY`.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the recent overlapping token-classifier fix and is already tied to the remaining policy boundary through issue history.
